column4: The successor's Theorem 2 proves a 3/2 bound for weakly stable half-matchings; an integral matching theorem for precisely the odd-preference-cycle class needs a rounding bridge. The original EGRES body timed out. Neither the paper's broad introductory wording nor fractional output clears that bridge.

Optimization over a capacitated perfect-matching polytope is not answered by invoking generic polynomial LP: both combinatorial and strongly polynomial are literal requirements. No complete combinatorial bridge established; EGRES source body unavailable.

A maximum-weight k-matching alone can fail extendability; optimizing a whole perfect matching can optimize the wrong k-edge subset. No polynomial selection/extension bridge established. Original body unavailable.

Two prescribed terminal pairs and minimum total length are essential; minimum-cost flow can pair the wrong terminals. No complete undirected disjoint-path optimization algorithm established. Original body unavailable.

Published Theorem 2 supplies randomized polynomial time for fixed k with nonnegative hyperedge costs. Section 3.3 proves the star-hedge partition-preserving reduction and running time; Remark 1 addresses costs. This is already public, while a deterministic interpretation is not cleared here.

Mixed fixed arcs and orientable edges couple the two paths; simply choosing shortest paths independently does not ensure compatible orientations. No polynomial joint-optimization bridge established. Original body unavailable.

Odd indegrees require parity constraints simultaneously with every directed cut's connectivity requirement. A parity-only orientation certificate does not characterize strong or k-edge connectivity. Original definitions/theorems unavailable.

All S-to-T terminal pairs, possibly overlapping sets, arbitrary k, minimum augmentation and strongly polynomial combinatorial time are simultaneous requirements. No full augmentation algorithm obtained; original body unavailable.

Cycle decompositions must avoid every consecutive transition of the specified Euler tour. A local splitting or an arbitrary cycle decomposition does not enforce that condition globally. No full construction or counterexample; original body unavailable.

The bases must be simultaneously disjoint and graph-independent; ordinary matroid base packing does not impose graph-independent color classes. No exchange argument proving the full 2Delta assertion; original body unavailable.

A staircase triangulation gives an upper bound, not the minimum for every dimension. Volume lower bounds do not close the gap or certify realizability of a minimal triangulation. No new all-dimensional mechanism.

The exponent must work for every n and every graph excluding the fixed induced H. A 5-cycle special case or stale open-status sentence does not answer all H. No uniform homogeneous-set mechanism; no live status claim.

The question asks for extremal discrepancy under each induced exclusion, not one large cut in a chosen graph. No matching universal bound and construction obtained; the interpretation of H and asymptotic sharpness must stay explicit.

A pair of colorings of one random graph or a numerical frequency is not an asymptotically almost sure nonuniqueness theorem. No probabilistic recoloring mechanism at the chromatic optimum established.

The inequality quantifies over arbitrary graphs and all relevant k. Trace and largest-eigenvalue bounds do not give the stated sum bound. No exact counterexample or universal majorization bridge found; current public status not cleared.

An arbitrary fixed pattern and arbitrary host size require an exact extremal packing answer. Layered constructions for selected patterns do not solve general permutation packing. No full-scope candidate.

The source itself prints n-1 for learning a linear ordering of all subsets. Arbitrary linear extensions versus additive/qualitative-probability orders are materially different models. An information-theoretic contradiction to the broad reading is a wording/model correction, not a qualified new outcome.

The source cites the symmetric grid regime n=exp(o(log m)); the target requires a wider high-probability statement for products of chains. No concentration argument with the needed unrestricted parameter control.
Two middle levels give a lower bound; a general matching upper bound for diamond-free families is the unresolved mechanism here. A few lattice levels or finite enumerations would be instances only.

Existence of the normalized limit is for every finite forbidden poset. Chain/Sperner estimates supply boundedness in familiar cases, not convergence for arbitrary P. No universal comparison between consecutive n obtained.

Irrationality or nonperiodicity does not force arbitrarily long zero blocks. The existential algebraic-number clause also needs its intended irrational/nontrivial domain clarified; rational examples are wording-only. No digit-distribution mechanism for sqrt(2).

At n=1 each reciprocal is at most 1, so the literal positive-integer statement fails because 4>3. This only repairs the standard n>=2 domain and earns no discovery credit. No full n>=2 construction obtained.

The source literally prints 2^R/n^R, incompatible with covering all 2^n words at fixed R. The elementary ball bound is |C|>=2^n/sum_{j=0}^R binom(n,j). Correcting the exponent is not a new sharp covering-density constant.

The same printed exponential factor issue occurs in the asymmetric covering problem. Directed Hamming balls and their overlap must be controlled to determine the optimal constant; a symmetric covering construction is insufficient. No full-scope bound.

The definition is asymmetric packing but the final sentence says largest asymmetric covering code. Without the packing condition all words give a trivial answer. Resolving this noun mismatch is uncredited; no exact optimal packing result.

The cyclic order must realize a covering family through overlapping windows. Arbitrary covering codes do not automatically give a cyclic string at the same size. No construction eliminating the source's logarithmic gap.

Substitution-instance counts are not ordinary contiguous block frequencies. A de Bruijn counterexample to a block-frequency implication would not address this definition. The source supplies no full substitution counting convention; no faithful mechanism qualified.

The record asks for exact Dedekind values for n>=10. An antichain recurrence without feasible exact evaluation does not supply those values. Wikipedia attribution is not the original counting-proof body; no expensive enumeration authorized or run.

The target is the unknown exact van der Waerden numbers, not improved lower bounds or a single previously known value. No exact value with matching lower/upper certificates qualified; the primary referenced integer-paper body was not fetched.

The July 2025 author problem and Gabrielov's actual generic-net definitions distinguish full arbitrary-angle classification from generic/integer-angle classes. Lemma 2.3's loop argument is local combinatorial input, not a full moduli/existence theorem. No extension covering all nongeneric angles.

Nadi v1 Theorem 1.1 already constructs, for each 0<s<1, an entire-function inverse germ with positive-capacity and positive H^s exceptional directions. The concluding proof uses two entire approximations, Rouche uniqueness and escaping inverse lifts. It blocks credit for that capacity/dimension route; it does not classify every possible finer exceptional-set theorem.

The October 16 2026 problem still distinguishes unrestricted Goldberg extremality from the double-one-point assumption. The context theorem determines the restricted single multiple-one-point threshold mu, not that every unrestricted extremal has this form. No reduction closing that gap.

The cached record adds f(0), derivative and max-modulus objectives not literally stated in the current two-page source. The latter instead uses the smallest hyperbolic disk of the zero and two one-points. Correspondence between these normalizations/objectives needs proof; the older restricted double-point theorem is insufficient.

The real-function restriction appears in current Problem 2, but the record's derivative and radial objectives need a precise source-normalization bridge. Known real/double-point context does not establish the full two-simple-point extremal problem.

Current Problem 3 requires one simple zero at 0 and two simple one-points at plus/minus ia. Replacing the pair by one double point invokes a different theorem. No exact threshold proof beyond already public context.

Current Problem 4 asks fixed rational degree versions. The known unrestricted holomorphic extremal in related context is transcendental; polynomial approximation changes degree and cannot establish fixed-degree optimum or classification.

Tao 2512.12455v2 Theorem 1.1(iv) already establishes the conjectured extremal for all sufficiently large degrees, so the asymptotic portion is public. The concluding Section 12 calculation absorbs O(||p||/C0) into a negative defect. It leaves no credited asymptotic shortcut; this review does not assert every small degree is resolved.

The October 3 2026 original body already gives generic single-input/output solvability and the m=p=2 obstruction, with the polynomial-matrix counterexample. Repackaging it, checking one pair or confusing real with complex pole placement earns no credit. No full classification for all pairs.

Original body separates primal MST counterexamples, dual dihedral-weighted MST speculation, simple edge unfoldings and creased uniqueness. A primal-MST or uncreased cube example already in the source does not answer the distinct quantified questions.

The November 1999 update already reports neighborly cubical four-polytopes with Omega(n log n) degenerate facets. Thus producing a witness to the 2n subquestion is no new outcome. The maximum for all n,d remains broader and is not solved here.

The body already gives joins of polygons and the five-dimensional asymptotic solution. Constant fatness examples do not prove superlinear four-dimensional complexity or higher-dimensional optimality. No new bound closing either full gap.

The no-K_{s,t} hypothesis is essential and the question varies n,m,d,s,t. Planar Szemeredi-Trotter or a known lower construction does not solve the general incidence maximum. No new full bound or counterexample to a precise asserted bound.

Original body supplies the k-level duality and multiple known bounds. A halving-line instance, old Dey upper bound or higher-dimensional lift is not the exact extremal answer. No mechanism matching upper and lower bounds uniformly.

The source separates tangencies with no triple meeting from transverse arrangements for digons; general position interpreted as no tangencies would trivialize only a wording variant. Pseudocircle equivalence is already stated; genuine-circle equivalence and exact bounds remain unproved here.

The source's spike/iron-maiden construction already gives quadratic lower bounds, and explicitly separates offsets, medial surfaces and line Voronoi diagrams. Reproducing that construction or using a polyhedral metric does not close the Euclidean upper gap for all three.

The request combines exact arbitrary-n Erdos-Szekeres numbers and empty polygon bounds. Source finite small-n examples and the record's acknowledged resolved empty-hexagon subproblem earn no new credit. No full arbitrary-n extremal mechanism.

The actual source index marks this problem Solved but supplies no linked proof body for that item. This is a public-resolution lead, not proof-level exclusion or renewed novelty clearance; hold until the exact complexity theorem/body is read.

Source explains why existing collinearity lower bounds use models unable to compute the minimum-area problem. Quoting them is not a lower bound in a suitable model; no new subquadratic algorithm or valid quadratic lower-bound transfer.

Real-plane quadratic algorithms and restricted-model lower bounds do not transfer to complex lines in C^2. The source explicitly warns of both gaps. No log-removal algorithm or suitable lower-bound mechanism obtained.

The fixed-d all-points-extreme decision problem is distinct from enumerating all faces. Output-sensitive hull enumeration alone does not improve the stated decision exponent. No new algorithm or matching lower bound in a specified model.
